newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Cyprus-registered group wins Svyazinvest stake.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus-registered group wins Svyazinvest stake.

text.p: Cyprus-registered Mustcom Ltd won a tender for 25 percent plus one share in Russian telecoms holding company Svyazinvest with a bid of $1.875 billion, a Russian Federal Property Fund official said on Friday.
He said Mustcom had been set up by Moscow investment bank Renaissance Capital and two other entities.

Earlier a spokesman for Russia's Uneximbank said the bank had won the stake in a consortium including its affiliates investment bank MFK (ICFI) and Interros Group, Renaissance Capital, and London-based Deutsche Morgan Grenfell with a $1.8 billion bid. The starting price for the stake had been $1.18 billion.
There was one other bid, from a Dutch-registered consortium called TeleFAM BV, fund deputy chairman Vladimir Malin told reporters.

It was not clear who was in TeleFAM but Russian agencies said the other bid was from a consortium comprising Russia's Alfa-Bank, Spain's Telefonica de Espana SA , international investment bank CS First Boston and an unknown individual investor.
Renaissance Capital and MFK -- the investment banking arm of Uneximbank and its Interros Group -- have announced that they intend to merge.
The sale of Svyazinvest, which has controlling stakes in 88 regional and other Russian telecoms companies, including long-distance operator Rostelekom , is Russia's biggest privatisation to date.
The government has said it will offer a further 24 percent to Russian investors later this year or next year, reducing its stake to 51 percent.
